story.title: Why this exists
story.p1: Every board comes with its own app, its own login and its own logbook. Climb a Kilter at your gym and a MoonBoard on holiday and you have two histories that never meet.
story.p2: Then one of those apps vanished overnight and climbers lost their logbooks with it. That is what happens when one company owns the only way into hardware you already paid for.
story.link: What happened, and how to get your data out

who.title: Who builds it
who.body: It started in 2024 with one climber and a repo, and it is still the kind of project people work on in the evenings. Bugs get found by someone standing at the wall, not by a QA team.

next.title: What's next
next.body: More boards, better offline, and getting your data out as easily as it went in. The roadmap is public and the arguments about it happen on Discord.

intro.title: Legal & Intellectual Property Policy
intro.p1: Boardsesh is a free, open-source, community-built alternative for browsing and interacting with standardised LED climbing training boards (Kilter Board, Tension Board, MoonBoard, and others). It is non-commercial and maintained entirely by volunteers.
intro.p2: We believe climbers should have the freedom to choose how they interact with hardware they've purchased, and that community-created data should remain accessible to the community.

facts.title: Climbs are factual data
facts.p1: A climb on a standardised board is a list of hold positions on a fixed, standardised layout (e.g. "start on A5, use B12, C3, D18, finish on K11"), combined with a grade and wall angle. This is factual, functional information — comparable to a chess position, a set of GPS coordinates, or a phone number — not a creative work of authorship.
facts.p2: Under U.S. copyright law, facts are not copyrightable (Feist Publications, Inc. v. Rural Telephone Service Co., 499 U.S. 340 (1991)). A standardised board with a finite number of holds (typically 200–500) produces climb definitions that are inherently constrained, factual, and functional.

community.title: The database is community-created
community.p1: The climb databases for these boards are almost entirely user-generated content. Individual climbers create and submit climbs. The board manufacturers did not author this content — they provide a platform for submission and display.
community.p2: The licensing position varies by manufacturer, but in no case does a manufacturer own the community's climb data:
community.aurora: Aurora Climbing (Kilter Board, Tension Board, and others): Aurora's Terms of Use grant them a "perpetual, unrestricted, unlimited, non-exclusive, irrevocable license" over user-submitted content. Crucially, this license is non-exclusive — it does not transfer ownership to Aurora, nor does it prevent the original creator (or third parties) from independently using, collecting, or presenting the same factual data.
community.moonBody: As of the last review of Moon Climbing's public-facing legal documents (February 2026), we did not find app-specific Terms of Service, an End User License Agreement, or a contributed-content license governing the MoonBoard app or its climb database. As with every board here, our position rests on the principle above: climb definitions are factual, functional data, and the databases are community-created.

compilation.title: Comprehensive databases have weak compilation protection
compilation.body: Even where a database arrangement might qualify for thin copyright protection as a compilation, the U.S. Supreme Court has held that protection extends only to creative selection or arrangement — not to the underlying facts. A database that comprehensively collects all user submissions without editorial curation (as these platforms do) is analogous to an alphabetical phone directory, which the Court found unprotectable in Feist.

attribution.title: Attribution & Respect for Creators
attribution.intro: We respect the climbing community and the people who create climbs.
attribution.item1: Where climb creator information is available, we attribute the creator by their username.
attribution.item2: We do not claim authorship of climbs we did not create.
attribution.item3Start: If you are the creator of a climb and would like it removed, please
attribution.item3End: or contact us and we will honour your request promptly.

interop.title: Interoperability & Hardware Compatibility
interop.intro: This project provides software and hardware designs that are compatible with standardised climbing board hardware. Climbers who have purchased these boards have a right to use third-party software and controllers with their own hardware.

software.title: Software interoperability
software.body: Our app communicates with board controllers over standard Bluetooth protocols. The Bluetooth communication protocol used by these boards is unencrypted and based on commodity hardware (WS2812B addressable LEDs driven by standard Bluetooth controllers). Implementing a compatible Bluetooth interface for the purpose of interoperability is well-established as lawful under both U.S. and EU law (Sega Enterprises Ltd. v. Accolade, Inc., 977 F.2d 1510 (9th Cir. 1992); EU Directive 2009/24/EC, Article 6).

controller.title: Open-source controller
controller.p1: This project also offers open-source controller hardware and firmware designs. The controller is an independent, original implementation that communicates using the same Bluetooth protocol as the official controllers. It is built on commodity components (standard microcontrollers and WS2812B LEDs) and does not incorporate any proprietary firmware, code, or hardware designs from any board manufacturer. No patents are known to exist covering the LED controller systems used by any current board manufacturer.
controller.p2: Our controller is designed to be interoperable with both this project's software and, at the user's discretion, official manufacturer apps. Any such interoperability is initiated by the end user on their own hardware.

hostedService.title: Hosted service and API access
hostedService.p1: Boardsesh's code is open source under the Apache 2.0 licence. That licence covers the code. It does not cover the hosted service: the accounts, climb database, logbook sync and real-time servers that the Boardsesh apps and website connect to. We run and pay for those.
hostedService.p2Start: The public API documented on the
hostedService.p2End: is for integrations: tools that read climb data, or act on behalf of a signed-in climber from their own account, within the rate limits the service applies.
hostedService.p3: The hosted service is not a backend for other apps. A publicly distributed app or fork that uses Boardsesh accounts, data or servers as its service needs our written permission, and we do not currently grant it. If you fork Boardsesh, run your own backend too. The code is there for exactly that. The development setup in CONTRIBUTING.md is the starting point today; official self-hosting docs are still to come.
hostedService.p4Start: You do not have to start from an empty database either. The
hostedService.p4End: are public SQLite files of the climb catalogs, cheap for us to serve, and you are welcome to use them. We are also happy to talk about syncing non-user data such as climbs and grades to an alternative service.

trademark.title: Trademark Usage
trademark.body: We use board and product names (e.g. "Kilter Board", "MoonBoard", "Tension Board") solely to describe hardware compatibility and interoperability. These names are trademarks of their respective owners. This project is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Aurora Climbing, Moon Climbing, or any board manufacturer.

dmca.title: DMCA & Takedown Requests
dmca.intro: We take intellectual property concerns seriously. If you believe any material in this project infringes your copyright, please contact us with the following information:
dmca.item1: Identification of the copyrighted work you believe is infringed.
dmca.item2: Identification of the material you believe is infringing, with enough detail for us to locate it.
dmca.item3: Your contact information (name, address, email, phone number).
dmca.item4: A statement that you have a good faith belief that the use is not authorised by the copyright owner, its agent, or the law.
dmca.item5: A statement, under penalty of perjury, that the information in your notice is accurate and that you are the copyright owner or authorised to act on their behalf.
dmca.review1: We will review all valid requests promptly and in good faith. We may also file a counter-notice where we believe a takedown request is based on a misidentification of the material or a misunderstanding of the law.

community.title: A Note to the Community
community.p1: The climbing community has a long tradition of openly sharing beta. This project exists in that spirit. We are not trying to harm any company — we are trying to give climbers better tools to interact with hardware they already own and data they helped create.
community.p2: Manufacturers continue to benefit from this ecosystem. Our project drives demand for their physical products (holds, boards, panels) where they provide genuine value. We simply believe climbers deserve a choice in how they interact with their hardware.
community.p3: If you are a board manufacturer and would like to discuss collaboration or have concerns, we welcome open dialogue. Please reach out.

legal.footer: This document is provided for informational purposes and does not constitute legal advice. Last updated: 10-08-2026

install.title: Get the app
install.intro: Lighting the wall, logging sends and crew sessions all happen in the app.

hero.title: Put a climb on your board
hero.subtitle: A tap previews a climb. Put on board lights it, and the wall follows your picks for a while.

connect.title: Put a climb on the wall
connect.lead: A tap shows you the climb. Put on board connects if needed and lights it.
connect.clipAlt: Tapping Put on board starts a timed drive, shown by a clock and shrinking frost
connect.clipCaption: Tap Put on board. The clock starts, and each new climb you pick refills it.
connect.step1: In a climb, tap the large Put on board button.
connect.step2: First time only, pick your board from the list. Don't see it? Tap Search for any board.
connect.step3: Allow Bluetooth when asked. Android asks for Nearby devices, or Location on Android 11 and older.
connect.otherBoard: A climb from another board at your gym shows Put on Tension, or that board's name. Tap it to move there and light the climb.
connect.changeBoard: At a different wall? Change board is the first row behind your avatar.

driving.title: Driving the wall
driving.lead: When you are driving the wall, every climb you pick lights at once.
driving.looking: Otherwise a tap opens a preview, and the wall keeps its climb.
driving.way1: Put on board lights the climb, then drives for a set time: 45 seconds unless you change it. Each pick restarts the clock.
driving.way2: Swipe the wall button left until it reads Let go to light every climb, then let go. Or, once connected, hold it and pick Light every climb. You drive until you tap You are driving the wall.
driving.way3: Turn on Always drive the wall in Settings, then Board. Whenever your phone holds the board, you drive. A tap pauses it until the board disconnects or you tap Put on board.
driving.tell: A frosted wall button reading You are driving the wall means you are driving.
driving.tellClock: A clock beside the label means a timed drive, and the frost shrinks as time runs out. No clock means it lasts until you tap. On the mini player, the bulb turns amber while you drive.
driving.clipAlt: Swiping the wall button left to start driving, then tapping it to stop
driving.clipCaption: Swipe left and let go to light every climb. Tap You are driving the wall to stop.
driving.end1: You tap You are driving the wall.
driving.end2: The clock runs out. Timed drives only.
driving.end3: A crewmate puts a climb up. Timed drives only.
driving.end4: You tap Turn off all lights, the connection drops, or you switch boards or sessions.
driving.after: After a drive, your next pick opens as a preview again.

states.lookingAlt: Player showing a preview: the top bar reads Preview · not on the wall and the button reads Put on board
states.lookingCaption: Looking: Put on board. Nothing lights until you tap it.
states.timedAlt: Player while driving with a clock: the button reads You are driving the wall · 0:28
states.timedCaption: Timed drive: the clock counts down after Put on board.
states.openAlt: Player while driving with no clock: the button reads You are driving the wall
states.openCaption: Swipe to drive: no clock, it lights until you tap.

history.title: What's on the wall now
history.lead: Board history lists every climb this wall has lit, whoever lit it, newest first.
history.p1: Tap the clock in the Climbs header to open it. Tap a climb to preview it. Your queue's History is a separate list.
history.p2: The Climbs header capsule shows the wall's climb while a connected phone has it lit, or for an hour after it went up. You can hide it until a different climb goes up.

controls.title: Board controls and settings
controls.lead: While connected, hold the wall button to open Board controls.
controls.shotAlt: Board controls for a connected board
controls.shotCaption: Re-light, turn off all lights or disconnect.
controls.lightingShotAlt: Board lighting settings with drive duration and automatic lighting controls
controls.lightingShotCaption: Settings, then Board: when driving stops.
controls.row1: Stop driving after. Change the drive time, or pick Right away.
controls.row2: Re-light board. Sends the climb to the LEDs again.
controls.row3: Turn off all lights. This also stops driving.
controls.row4: Disconnect board. Use it when you connected to the wrong wall.
controls.row5: Light the hold above. MoonBoard only.
controls.settingsIntro: Settings, then Board holds the rest:
controls.setting1: Stop driving after: Right away, 30 seconds up to 5 minutes, or Until I stop.
controls.setting2: Always drive the wall: off by default.
controls.setting3: Disconnect Bluetooth when driving ends: off by default. It frees the board for the next climber.
controls.setting4: In a session too: on by default. It lets you drive in a crew.
controls.bulb: Prefer a lightbulb? Set Board control to Lightbulb under ⋯, View options, Buttons.

control.title: When another phone has the board
control.lead: A Kilter or Tension board talks to one phone at a time, and a new connection drops the old one.
control.p1: MoonBoard V3+ takes several phones. The original MoonBoard box keeps the first phone, and may need a controller restart.
control.p2: In a crew, only the phone holding the board connects. Your Put on board goes through that phone, and its face shows on your wall button.

liveActivity.title: Lock screen and Dynamic Island
liveActivity.lead: Start a session, alone is fine, and your lock screen gets board controls.
liveActivity.p1: On iPhone, a Live Activity shows the climb on the wall and its grade. While your phone holds the board it adds Previous, Next and a lightbulb that re-lights the wall.
liveActivity.p2: Next steps your queue, not the list you were swiping, and lights that climb at once. Like Put on board, it starts or extends a drive.
liveActivity.p3: Android shows the same controls in a notification. Locking the screen never disconnects the board.

failed.title: Board won't connect?
failed.lead: The Couldn't connect alert names the problem.
failed.fix1: Couldn't find your board. Check it's on and you're near it. If another phone is connected, disconnect there first.
failed.fix2: Couldn't connect. Move closer and try again.
failed.fix3: Connected, but the board didn't respond. Turn the board off and on.
failed.fix4: Bluetooth is off. Turn it on.
failed.fix5: On Android, if nothing is found, tap Allow Location or Turn on Location at the bottom of the sheet.
failed.twoBoards: Two boards in range? Yours is listed first. Read the serial before you tap. A Board configuration doesn't match alert means the controller has a different setup. Pick Cancel, Connect anyway or Switch board setup.
failed.duplicate: Same board listed twice? Two serials are two controllers. A row reading only Kilter Board is a newer LED box, and more signal bars usually means your wall. If the wrong wall lights, tap Disconnect board in Board controls.
failed.duplicateYourBoards: A board twice under Your boards is different. Tap Edit, then Delete or Unfollow.

hero.title: Find, play and save climbs
hero.subtitle: Filter the list, swipe through it, press and hold for more, and save climbs to playlists.

player.title: Swipe through a list
player.lead: A tap previews a climb, and swiping walks the list you tapped it from.
player.p1: The top bar says Preview · not on the wall and names the list, like Search results · 4 of 23. The wall, your queue and everyone else's phone stay as they were.
player.p2: From the climb on the wall, swipes go to Up next first. Then they carry on into the list that climb came from, which the queue sheet shows under Then from and the list's name. The end of the list shows an end card.
player.p3: The back chip takes you to the climb on the wall. The mini player is your last look: tap it to reopen that preview with its list.
player.p4: In a crew, the top bar says Only you see this, and each phone walks its own list.
player.callout: Put on board makes a previewed climb the wall's climb. While you are driving the wall there is no preview: every pick lights at once.
player.clipAlt: Swiping through a list in the player
player.clipCaption: Swipe through the list. The wall keeps its climb.

menu.title: Press and hold a climb
menu.lead: Press and hold a climb row for every action on that climb.
menu.p1: Tap an action, or tap outside to close. Log a tick, Add to Playlist and Share are the ones you will use most.
menu.playNext: Play next puts the climb at the top of Up next. Play last puts it at the bottom.
menu.favorite: Toggle favorite saves the climb to Liked Climbs. Once it's there, the row reads Remove favorite.
menu.remix: Remix this climb starts a new climb from these holds.
menu.edit: Edit climb works on your own climbs, as a draft or within 24 hours of publishing.
menu.others: Add beta video, Edit logbook entry, Open in Aurora app and Report climb show up when they apply.
menu.p2: Prefer a tap? Turn on Show quick-actions button under Settings, then Climbs & grades, then Climb list. Every row gets a ⋮ that opens the same menu.
menu.clipCaption: Hold the row and the menu opens on its own.

filters.title: Filter by grade, hold, region or setter
filters.lead: Open Filters on the Climbs tab. A pin next to a filter's name turns it into a chip above the list.
filters.grade: Tap Grade, then a grade. Tap a second grade within three seconds for a range, or the selected grade again to clear.
filters.angle: Grades and send counts use the board's angle. Tap the degrees chip to change it.
filters.progress: Signed in, the Progress chips use your history. Unsent hides your sends, Projects keeps climbs tried but not sent, and Not tried keeps climbs never logged.
filters.gradeClipCaption: Two quick taps build a range.
filters.holdsIntro: To filter by hold, scroll to The climb in Filters and tap Hold types.
filters.holdStep3: Pinch to zoom, then tap holds. Tap again with the same brush to clear a mark.
filters.holdNote: Clear all wipes the board. MoonBoard has no Foot brush.
filters.holdClipCaption: Pick a brush first, then tap holds.
filters.region: To box off part of the wall, tap Board region, then Add a region. Drag the middle to move the box and a corner to resize it.
filters.regionModes: All holds keeps climbs entirely inside the box. Any hold keeps climbs that reach into it.
filters.regionClipCaption: Drag the middle to move the box, a corner to resize it.
filters.setters: Tap Follow on a setter's page or on the Setters screen. Then turn on Climbs by people I follow, just below Setters.
filters.settersPicker: On the Setters screen, check a box to filter or tap a name to browse their climbs.
filters.shotCaption: Check a box to filter. Tap a name to browse.
filters.count: The button at the bottom shows how many climbs match. Reset clears every filter.

rows.title: Swipe a climb row
rows.lead: Swipe right to play a climb next, or left to add it to a playlist.
rows.p2: The small glyph is your history: a bolt for flashed, a circled tick for sent, a circled cross for tried, a circled C for benchmark.
rows.clipCaption: Right plays it next. Left opens the playlist picker.

playlists.title: Playlists
playlists.lead: A playlist is a saved list of climbs for one board, and you walk it with swipes.
playlists.step1: Open Discover and check the board pill at the top.
playlists.step2: Tap the plus, name it, pick a color and tap Create.
playlists.step3: Add climbs: swipe a row left, or press and hold it and tap Add to Playlist.
playlists.p1: Your playlist appears under My Playlists. The picker only shows playlists for the climb's board and layout.
playlists.play: To play a playlist, tap a climb in it and swipe. The play button in the header starts from the first climb.
playlists.remove: To take a climb out, open Add to Playlist on it and tap the ticked playlist. Or tap the pencil on the playlist, tap the red minus and confirm.
playlists.reorder: Drag the handle to reorder. For You lists have no edit mode, so un-heart a climb or log the send instead.
playlists.removeClipCaption: Tap a ticked playlist and the climb comes back out.
playlists.forYou: Discover builds eight For You lists: Crowd Favorites, Hidden Gems, At Your Level, Fresh, Five Stars, Most Repeated, Projects and Liked Climbs.
playlists.forYouHow: The first four read your board at your angle and skip your sends. The last four come from your ticks and hearts.
playlists.tags: To see which playlists a climb is in, turn on Show playlist tags under Settings, then Climbs & grades, then Climb list.
playlists.browse: Browse public playlists on the web
playlists.discoverShotCaption: Pinned, then My Playlists, then For You.

diagram.description: Where a swipe goes in the player. Open a climb from a list and swiping shows the climb before or after it in that list, without lighting anything. Put on board lights a preview. From the climb on the wall, swiping goes to Up next first, then the list it came from, then an end card.
diagram.listCaption: Tap a climb in a list: swipes walk that list. Nothing lights.
diagram.wallCaption: From the climb on the wall: Up next first, then the list it came from.

hero.title: Help
hero.subtitle: Short guides for the app, how to bring your Kilter or Tension logbook across, and where to ask.

guides.title: Guides
guides.lead: Pick the guide that matches what you're doing.

start.title: Board and Bluetooth
start.body: Put a climb on the wall, drive it, and fix a board that won't connect.

browse.title: Find, play and save climbs
browse.body: Swipe through lists, filter by grade or hold, and build playlists.

crew.title: Climb with your crew
crew.body: Start a session and invite your crew with a QR code.

logbook.title: Your logbook
logbook.body: Log and edit sends, and attach beta videos.

spray.title: Spraywalls
spray.body: Photograph your Spraywall and fix the holds Boardsesh finds.

bring.title: Bring your Kilter or Tension logbook
bring.lead: Link your board account once and your sends come across.

counts.title: Why does Kilter's app show more climbs?
counts.lead: Both apps have the same climbs and count them differently.
counts.item1: Boardsesh counts each climb once. Kilter's app appears to count a climb once per angle it has been climbed at.
counts.item2: On an 8x12 Kilter home wall that is about 18,000 climbs in Boardsesh and about 36,000 in Kilter's app.

ask.title: Ask a question
ask.lead: Discord is the fastest place to get an answer.

hero.title: Your logbook and beta videos
hero.subtitle: Tick a climb at the wall, fix it later, and attach your beta video.

log.title: Log it at the wall
log.lead: Tap the tick, fill in what you want, and save.
log.shotCaption: The tick opens the log sheet.
log.logbookShotCaption: Swipe right to edit, left to delete.
log.p1: Tap the big tick in the play drawer, or ✓ on the bar at the bottom. Date and Time are filled in, and the rest is optional.
log.p2: Attempt logs a go that didn't stick. The other button reads Flash on your first go at this angle, otherwise Send. Ticks save offline and sync later.

edit.title: Edit or delete an entry
edit.lead: Swipe a logbook row right to edit it, or left to delete it.
edit.clipCaption: A short swipe shows the pencil or the bin.
edit.p1: Open the Profile tab, then Logbook. Pressing and holding a row offers Edit logbook entry too.
edit.p2: You can change Status, Angle, Tries, Grade, Stars and Note. Edits need a connection.
edit.p3: To delete, swipe the row left, or tap Delete this ascent in the edit sheet. It asks first, and there is no undo. Comments and votes on that ascent go too.

repeats.title: One row per climb, day and angle
repeats.lead: Your logbook keeps one row per climb, per day, per angle.
repeats.p1: Four goes tonight are one row, with tries added up and your best result showing. Mirrored goes get their own row.
repeats.p2: Filter sorts by Latest or Hardest and narrows by status, grade, angle, date and Benchmarks only.

bring.title: Bring your Kilter or Tension logbook
bring.lead: Link your board account once and your sends come across.
bring.step1: Tap your avatar, then Settings, then Connected apps.
bring.step2: Under Board accounts, tap Link on the Tension card or Sign in to Kilter on the Kilter card.
bring.step3: Enter that board's username and password.
bring.p1: Used the old Kilter app? The Kilter (Aurora) card takes a JSON export.
bring.p2: Sync runs one way, from their apps into Boardsesh, about every 12 hours. Nothing goes back.

beta.title: Attach a beta video
beta.lead: Boardsesh links Instagram reels and TikToks to climbs.
beta.step1: On your reel or TikTok, tap Share and pick Boardsesh. In Instagram it can hide under More.
beta.step2: Boardsesh opens Attach your beta, with your logged climbs below the post.
beta.step3: Tap the climb the video shows.
beta.callout: There is no confirm step and no way to remove a video, so check the climb name first.
beta.p1: The climb must be in your logbook as a send or an attempt. Only public Instagram and TikTok links work.
beta.p2: To film new beta, press and hold a climb and choose Add beta video. Tap Copy caption, then Open Instagram, and post with that caption.
beta.p3: Keep the quoted climb name in it, since that matches the reel. MoonBoard captions have no quotes, so pick the climb yourself.

findBeta.title: Watch others' beta
findBeta.lead: Open a climb and scroll down to Beta Videos.
findBeta.p1: Tap a card to open it in Instagram or TikTok. To list only climbs with beta, turn on Beta videos only in Filters.
findBeta.p2: Your own beta sits at the bottom of Progress on the Profile tab.

next.title: Keep going
next.climbMenu: Log a tick from any list

hero.title: Climb with your crew
hero.subtitle: Start a session, share the link, and climb on one board together.

start.title: Start a session
start.lead: Every session starts from the Session tab.
start.step1: Open the Session tab. Check the board at the top.
start.step2: Show this session live lets your crew find and join it. Off, only your invite link works.
start.step3: Tap Start, then Invite climbers for a QR code, Copy link and Share.
start.shotCaption: Who has joined and what's lit.
start.liveShotCaption: Climbing now on the Home tab lists sessions you can join.

join.title: Join a session
join.lead: Scan the host's code, or find a session nearby.
join.way1: Scan the host's QR code or open their link.
join.way2: On the Home tab, look under Climbing now.
join.way3: Tap the board at the top of the Climbs tab, then Climbing here now.
join.p1: Each opens a Join Sam's session? card. Tap Join session.

wall.title: Who lights the wall
wall.lead: One phone holds the board, and everyone else lights climbs through it.
wall.p1: Tap Put on board. The holder's phone lights it, and their face shows on your wall button.
wall.busy: If a crewmate put a climb up while you were looking, Put on board asks first. Keep theirs leaves it lit. Put mine up replaces it.
wall.queue: Anyone can add, reorder or remove queued climbs. Only the climber who started the session can end it. Everyone else taps Leave session.

browsing.title: Browse without moving the wall
browsing.lead: In a crew every tap is a preview that only you see.
browsing.p1: Swipes walk your own list and never move the wall. The back chip, with the face of whoever lit the wall, returns you to its climb.
browsing.drivingLink: Only the phone holding the board can drive it. See how driving works.

history.title: After the session
history.lead: Your profile's Sessions tab lists every session with its climbs and sends.
history.p1: The end-of-session summary has Save to Apple Health and Share to Strava. Connected apps in Settings automates it.

hero.title: Set up your Spraywall
hero.subtitle: Every hold and climb is set on one photo of your Spraywall, so the shot matters.

watch.title: Watch the walkthrough
watch.lead: Boardsesh finds the holds in your photo, so a good shot means fewer to fix.
watch.videoAlt: Adding a Spraywall and editing its holds in the Boardsesh app

photo.title: Taking the photo
photo.lead: Five habits give the hold finder a clean photo.
photo.square: Stand square on, in line with the Spraywall's middle. From the side, far holds shrink.
photo.portrait: Hold the phone in portrait and shoot at 1x. Landscape shrinks holds to a strip.
photo.tilt: Tilt the phone to match the Spraywall's angle, parallel to its face.
photo.frame: Get the whole Spraywall in frame. If it doesn't fit, step back instead of using the wide lens.
photo.lighting: Use bright, even light so the holds stand out.
photo.exampleAlt: An indoor Spraywall photographed square on, with every hold in frame
photo.exampleCaption: Whole Spraywall in frame, shot square on.

add.title: Add the Spraywall
add.lead: Take a photo, let Boardsesh scan for holds, then name it.
add.step2: Take or choose a photo. Use Crop or rotate to tidy its edges.
add.step3: Pin the four corners to unlock other backgrounds, or skip to keep the photo.
add.step4: Let Boardsesh scan the photo, then review the hold rings.
add.step5: Swipe to pick a background and how holds light up. Without corner pins, Photo is the only background.
add.p1: Last, name the Spraywall and set its angle, then publish. The angle is fixed once you publish.

fix.title: Fix holds before you publish
fix.lead: Boardsesh shows the holds it found as rings. Check them before anyone climbs.
fix.select: Select: tap a hold to move, resize or switch it off.
fix.add: Add: mark a missed hold with Draw or Corners.
fix.trace: Trace: redraw the selected hold's outline in one loop.
fix.refine: Refine: brush along the outline to grow or shrink it.
fix.join: Join: select a hold, then tap another to merge their outlines.
fix.imageAlt: Spraywall editor with a selected hold and the five tools
fix.imageCaption: Select a ring to see its controls.
fix.maybe: Dashed rings are uncertain. Tap one, then tap Keep.
fix.toggle: Tap a ring to select it, and tap again to switch it off. You can switch it back on or delete it.
fix.longPress: Press and hold a ring to move it, or bare Spraywall to place a new hold.
fix.gestures: Pan with two fingers and pinch to zoom. Undo and Redo step through your edits.
fix.videoAlt: Adding missed holds, correcting outlines and publishing hold changes
fix.missed1: Pinch to zoom in on the missed hold.
fix.missed2: Choose Add, then Draw. Draw a closed outline around the hold, or tap for a circle.
fix.missed3: Repeat for other missed holds. Undo if you slip.
fix.corners: For straight edges, choose Add, then Corners. Tap at least three points around the hold, then tap Finish.
fix.drawAlt: Add tool in Draw mode with an outlined hold
fix.drawCaption: Add, Draw: outline one missed hold.
fix.cornersAlt: Add tool in Corners mode with points around a hold
fix.cornersCaption: Add, Corners: three or more points, then Finish.

edit.title: Edit holds later
edit.lead: You can add or fix holds any time. Adding holds leaves existing climbs unchanged.
edit.p1: On Boards, tap your Spraywall to make it active. Tap the magnifying-glass Climbs tab, then the Spraywall name at the top. Tap Edit holds, and finish with Publish holds.
edit.p2: If your edits remove a hold that published climbs use, Boardsesh asks you to confirm. Keep holds cancels. Remove anyway publishes.
edit.p3: Those climbs stay, with a missing-hold warning, and so do their logged ascents. Moving, resizing, reshaping or joining a hold does the same.
edit.p4: Tap Remix on an affected climb to set an updated copy. It does not repair the original.
edit.p5: If the holds changed across the Spraywall, tap Reset this Spraywall in the same sheet and start from a new photo. Publishing archives the old Spraywall with its climbs.

pencil.title: Apple Pencil on iPad
pencil.lead: In the full-width iPad editor, Apple Pencil draws and toggles holds.
pencil.p1: Draw around an unmarked hold to add its outline, or tap an unmarked spot for a circle. Tap a marked hold to switch it on or off.
pencil.p2: Pencil turns on when it first touches or hovers over the editor, unless you chose a setting. With Pencil only on, fingers still select, move and pan.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro1: Boardsesh is an open-source app for controlling climbing training boards (Kilter, Tension, MoonBoard) over Bluetooth. This policy explains what data we collect, why, and what we do with it.
privacy.intro2ProductAnalytics: The short version: we collect only what we need to make the app work. We do not sell your data, there are no ads in Boardsesh, and we do not share data with data brokers. We do advertise Boardsesh on Reddit and Instagram, and on our website analytics includes measuring those ads with Meta and Reddit, as described below.

collect.title: What we collect
collect.accountBody: When you create an account, we store your email address and username. Your email is used for authentication. Your username is displayed on your profile and visible to other users in Party Mode sessions and social features.
collect.activityBody: When you log a send or attempt, we store the climb details, grade, date, and any notes you add. This powers your logbook and progression tracking.
collect.locationBody: If you grant location permission, we use your approximate location to help you discover nearby Party Mode sessions. We do not track your location in the background or store location history.
collect.productAnalyticsBody: We use PostHog for feature usage, page views, performance and optional session replay in the app. In the EU, the EEA, the UK, Switzerland, Gibraltar, Jersey, Guernsey, the Isle of Man, China, South Korea, Andorra, Monaco, San Marino, Vatican City, the Faroe Islands and Quebec, and whenever we cannot tell where you are, we ask first and PostHog runs only after you allow analytics. Elsewhere analytics is on by default, under our legitimate interest in improving Boardsesh, and you can turn it off anytime in Settings or Privacy choices; if your browser sends a Global Privacy Control signal, we treat it as a no. We decide this from the country and, in Canada, province Cloudflare reports for your connection, which we do not store. Signed-in analytics can be linked to your Boardsesh account. Install attribution needs your own Allow everywhere; the default does not turn it on. With your Allow, Android install attribution may include the Play Store install referrer and campaign information, and on iOS we use Apple AdServices through our own backend to measure which Apple Ads campaigns lead to signups and climbing activity. We share validated campaign identifiers and download status with PostHog, never the attribution token. We do not use these data to show you ads.
collect.adMeasurementBody: We advertise Boardsesh on Reddit and Instagram. When analytics is on for our website, we load the Meta Pixel and the Reddit Pixel so Meta and Reddit can tell us which ads bring visitors and app store taps. They receive the pages you visit on boardsesh.com, your taps on our app store buttons (which store, and where the button was) and what their pixels read from your browser: your IP address, browser details and their own cookies. We never send them your email, your account or any other contact details. In the regions where we ask first, this needs an Allow given after our banner started naming Meta and Reddit. Elsewhere it follows the analytics default and stops when you say no in Privacy choices or your browser sends a Global Privacy Control signal. It never runs in the app, on kiosk displays, in embedded widgets or on sign-in pages.
collect.serviceStatsBody: We record a signed-in account’s active day and platform in our own database, regardless of analytics consent, under legitimate interest to understand service use. These rows are kept for 13 months. Only aggregate daily, weekly and monthly counts are sent to PostHog. Signed-out visitors are not included in these account-based active-user counts.

bluetooth.title: Bluetooth
bluetooth.body: Boardsesh uses Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) to connect to your climbing board's LED controller. The Bluetooth connection is used exclusively to send hold lighting commands to the board. No personal data is transmitted over Bluetooth. The app does not read data from the board beyond basic device identification during pairing.

location.title: Location data
location.body1: Location access is optional. When granted, it is used for one purpose: making your Party Mode session discoverable to nearby climbers. Your location is shared with the server only while a Party Mode session is active. We do not store your location history, build a location profile, or share location data with anyone outside of the party session discovery feature.
location.body2: You can revoke location permission at any time in your device settings. The app works fully without it.

sprayPhotos.title: Spraywall photos
sprayPhotos.body1: When you add a Spraywall, we keep its photo and the holds you mark. Who can see the photo follows the Spraywall's visibility setting: private, link-only or public. Members of a gym can also see the Spraywalls attached to that gym.
sprayPhotos.body2: Each Spraywall has a “Help train hold finding” switch. While it is on, we use the Spraywall's photo and the holds you mark to train the hold finder, the part of the app that spots holds in a new Spraywall photo. A Boardsesh admin checks them first to make sure they are good to learn from. That applies at every visibility, private Spraywalls included. The copy we use for training is kept in private storage and is never shared or published outside Boardsesh.
sprayPhotos.body3: The switch is on when you add a Spraywall, and you can change it then or any time later under Edit board. Spraywalls added before the switch existed, or with a version of the app that does not show it, start with it off. We train on a Spraywall whose switch is on under legitimate interest to improve hold finding; switching it off is how you object, and it takes effect as described below.
sprayPhotos.body4: Switching it off, deleting the Spraywall, or deleting your account takes the Spraywall out of our stored training set within 24 hours. A copy already downloaded for a training run can be used for up to 7 more days, and is deleted the next time we fetch the set. Models we already trained keep what they learned, but they hold no copy of your photo.
sprayPhotos.body5: If a Spraywall is reported, a Boardsesh admin can see its photo to review the report, whatever the switch says. When you delete a Spraywall, we delete its photo after 30 days. When you delete your account, your Spraywall photos are deleted with it; a training copy leaves on the timing above. Resetting a Spraywall keeps the old one, photo included, as an archived Spraywall until you delete it too. Turning the switch off on either Spraywall covers both.

connectedApps.title: Apps you connect
connectedApps.intro: You can connect another app to your Boardsesh account, such as a training planner. Before anything is shared, Boardsesh shows you the app, who makes it, a link to its privacy policy and what it asks to see. Nothing is shared until you choose Allow.
connectedApps.whatItGets: Depending on what you allow, the app can see your display name and profile photo, and every tick in your logbook, including ticks you keep to “Only me”. Each tick comes with the climb it is on: its name, grade, board and layout. That includes a climb someone else set that is still a draft or unlisted, because the tick is part of your logbook. On someone else’s Spraywall that isn’t public, the app gets your tick but not the climb’s name or the Spraywall’s name.
connectedApps.afterSharing: Once the app has your data, the app’s own privacy policy covers what it does with it.
connectedApps.disconnect: You can disconnect an app at any time in your Boardsesh settings. Any change to your password, including resetting it or setting one for the first time, disconnects every app. After that the app can’t read anything new. Disconnecting, or deleting your Boardsesh account, does not delete what the app already copied: ask the app to delete it.

thirdParty.title: Third-party services
thirdParty.posthogBody: PostHog processes optional product analytics and app session replay in the United States. We also send minimal operational events without account identifiers for service stability, kiosk displays and update health, plus aggregate active-user counts. See
thirdParty.adPixelsBody: Meta Platforms and Reddit receive ad-measurement data from our website while analytics is on (see What we collect). They also use it under their own privacy policies, which can include processing in the United States. See
thirdParty.auroraBody: If you link your Aurora Climbing account (used by Kilter and Tension boards), we sync your climb data with Aurora's servers so your logbook stays consistent across apps. This sync only happens when you initiate it. See
thirdParty.hostingBody: We use Railway for application and database hosting, and Cloudflare for content delivery, browser-app hosting and media storage. These providers process requests needed to deliver Boardsesh. See
thirdParty.sentryBody: We use Sentry for error monitoring under legitimate interest to keep Boardsesh working. Default personal-information collection is disabled; error reports are limited and sensitive fields are removed. This service remains on when analytics is declined. See
thirdParty.expoBody: We use Expo Observe for performance timings, device/build information and error diagnostics on our own server, under legitimate interest to keep Boardsesh working. Diagnostics remain on when analytics is declined. SDK installation and session identifiers support update health; we assign no Boardsesh account identity to Observe. See
thirdParty.stripeBody: If you give through our support page, Stripe handles the payment. Stripe receives your card or wallet details, your email address, your billing country and any name or address you enter at checkout. Boardsesh never sees your full card number. We see your email, any name you enter, the amount, your billing country (plus postcode or address when checkout asks for one), your card brand, its last 4 digits and expiry, and a short tag for the page you came from. We use this to carry out the payment you asked for, send receipts and answer questions, and we keep it because tax law requires payment records. The legal basis is performing the payment you asked for and our legal duty to keep those records. A name you enter may be shown when we thank supporters; leave it blank to stay anonymous. See

sharing.title: Data sharing
sharing.body1ProductAnalytics: We do not sell your data, show ads in Boardsesh or share information with data brokers. The providers described above process data for hosting, storage, payments, service reliability and optional analytics, which on our website includes ad measurement with Meta and Reddit. Aurora Climbing synchronization runs when you enable it.
sharing.body2: Other Boardsesh users can see your username, profile, and logged climbs if you participate in social features like Party Mode. This is visible in the app and is part of how the product works.
sharing.body3SprayPhotos: We do not give Spraywall photos or the holds you mark to anyone else to train on. The only model trained on them is our own hold finder. Other people see a Spraywall's photo as its visibility setting allows, and members of a gym see the Spraywalls attached to that gym, private ones included. A public Spraywall's photo is on the open web.

retention.title: Data retention
retention.body: We keep your account data and climb history for as long as your account is active. If you stop using Boardsesh, your data stays until you delete your account.
retention.donations: Donation records stay in Stripe and in our accounts for as long as tax law requires. They are not tied to your Boardsesh account, so deleting your account does not remove them. Questions about a donation record? Email us.

deletion.title: Account deletion
deletion.intro: You can delete your account and all associated data at any time. There are two ways to do it:
deletion.inAppBody: Tap your avatar, open Settings, then Account, and tap Delete account. You will be asked to confirm before anything is removed.
deletion.onWebBodyEnd: and open Settings, then Account, from your avatar menu to find the same Delete account button.
deletion.permanent: Deletion is immediate and permanent. Once confirmed, we remove your email address, username, logbook entries, queue data, and party session history from our servers. This cannot be undone.

children.title: Children
children.body: Boardsesh is not directed at children under 13. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 13. If you believe a child under 13 has created an account, contact us and we will delete it.

changes.title: Changes to this policy
changes.body: If we change this privacy policy, we will update this page with the new text and the "last updated" date. For significant changes, we may also notify you in the app.

contact.title: Contact
contact.body1Start: Questions about this policy or your data? Email us at
contact.body2Start: Boardsesh is open source. You can see exactly what data the app collects and how it is processed by reading the source code on

choices.title: Cookies and privacy choices
choices.storageBody: Required storage includes NextAuth login and sign-in-flow cookies, your language preference (boardsesh-locale), device preferences and the boardsesh-consent cookie. The consent cookie lasts one year and is shared between boardsesh.com and app.boardsesh.com. Outside the regions where we ask, the website sets it to the analytics default on your first visit. When analytics is on (your Allow, or the default outside the regions where we ask), PostHog stores identifiers and events (ph_* on the website and SDK storage in the app). Declining or withdrawing clears analytics identifiers and stops optional analytics, replay and install-attribution events. Basic crash and first-party performance diagnostics remain on. Feature flags still use an in-memory client; signed-in flags can use your account ID.
choices.adCookiesBody: While ad measurement is on, the Meta Pixel sets _fbp (and _fbc after you arrive from a Meta ad) and the Reddit Pixel sets _rdt_uuid (and _rdt_cid after you arrive from a Reddit ad), each for up to 90 days. Saying no in Privacy choices stops both pixels straight away and deletes these cookies.
choices.changeBody: Use Privacy choices in the website footer or Analytics in Settings → Privacy to change your answer. We save your decision on the device and, when signed in, on your account. Where analytics is on by default, that default stays on the device and is never saved to your account as consent. An account denial overrides device grants; an account grant fills devices that have not answered. We retain decision history as evidence of consent until account deletion. Anonymous, short-lived update-health and kiosk events remain enabled for service reliability.
